issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: Add ability to safely get the managed object from a ComWrappers CCW
comments: This should be done via your own `ComWrappers` implementation as opposed to relying upon it "magically" working. If we did this the API would need to throw if there wasn't a globally registered `ComWrappers` instance. One should really call [`ComWrappers.GetOrCreateObjectForComInstance()`](https://learn.microsoft.com//dotnet/api/system.runtime.interopservices.comwrappers.getorcreateobjectforcominstance).

> Using ComWrappers this isn't possible to do safely without adding an additional interface to the outgoing CCW. It would be good to add functionality to ComWrappers to query for a wrapped managed object on any IUnknown.

Which wrapper do you want? The `ComWrappers` mechanism is designed around a 1:N model - there are N potential CCWs, one for each `ComWrappers` implementation. It isn't possible to know which one is desired and would be incredibly expensive to create an API that permits this. Your implementation of `ComWrappers` should attempt to unwrap and if it can, it will, otherwise it is an native COM object and will be wrapped.

Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/interop-contrib See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation Using COM Interop it is a common pattern to cast incoming RCW's against internal instances. WinForms does this in a number of places. For example, we check incoming OLE control interfaces to see if they are our own hosting control and utilize fields/methods on the instance if it is. Using `ComWrappers` this isn't possible to do safely without adding an additional interface to the outgoing CCW. It would be good to add functionality to `ComWrappers` to query for a wrapped managed object on any `IUnknown`. Without a way for users to construct `ComWrappers` CCWs that we can attempt to unwrap when receiving from native methods they cannot enable trimming in their apps. ### API Proposal ```csharp namespace System.Runtime.InteropServices; public abstract class ComWrappers { public struct ComInterfaceDispatch { public static bool TryGetInstance(IUnknown* unknown, out T? instance) where T: class; } } ``` ### API Usage ```csharp public static MyCallbackApi(IUnknown* unknown) { if (ComWrappers.TryGetInstance(unknown, out MyObject? myObject) { // Do stuff } } ``` ### Alternative Designs We could potentially publish a new COM interface that we can have users implement in their `ComWrappers` CCWs that we can look for to know that it is ok to unwrap with `ComInterfaceDispatch.GetInstance`. ### Risks _No response_
Author: JeremyKuhne
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Runtime.InteropServices`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

> Without a way for users to construct ComWrappers CCWs that we can attempt to unwrap when receiving from native methods they cannot enable trimming in their apps.

See [`CreateObjectFlags.Unwrap`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.runtime.interopservices.createobjectflags), which will perform the unwrap for you instead of trying to do all this manually.

Spoke to @JeremyKuhne offline. I get this scenario now. The implementation here is a going to be more complicated than https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/79679, but is possible. In its simplest form, we can add a sentinel interface to the generated CCW and use that to return the associated `object` or perhaps the `GCHandle` that is embedded in the CCW.

Another alternative implementation is to do the same sort of check we have the diagnostics layer do (it checks if the QueryInterface implementation for the `IUnknown*` is one of the runtime-implemented ones). That way we'd be consistent throughout the stack (since the OOP diagnostics can't QI for a sentinel interface)

>That way we'd be consistent throughout the stack (since the OOP diagnostics can't QI for a sentinel interface)

The issue with this approach is that it breaks if user defined their own `IUnknown` methods. Having the diagnostic degrade is one thing but breaking core functionality is another. I'm not sure which is the best approach at the moment. My guess is we implement the QI first and see the performance cost.

What's the significance of the returned bool? Is that not redundant with `obj != null`? If yes, is this just to enable the C# `out var` syntax? Seems drastic to add a strictly unneeded return value just for that.
The existing API on Marshal has "get or create"-semantics (which would never return `null`). I think the goal was to differentiate the semantics more strongly via API shape.

review_comments: It looks like we don't add to the cache when `CreateObjectFlags.UniqueInstance` is set, so I think `TryGetComInstance` won't work for those objects.
Maybe also add a test for this?

Not directly related to this PR, but I found it confusing that `ManagedObjectWrapper` in coreclr puts the runtime-defined entries first, then the user-defined ones, but nativeaot puts user-defined first, then runtime-defined.

That is a fair point. This is another example of the trouble with having multiple implementations. I filed https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/77738 to consider having CoreCLR use the NativeAOT implementation. Unsure if that is feasible but if that were to happen the above should be inverted to match the CoreCLR approach.
